rfi.title: School students called to join Yellow Vests and unions for mass French protest
rfi.description: Following an unsuccessful meeting with France's education minister on Thursday, protesting high school pupils across the country say they will not let up the pressure on the government. The Yellow Vests movement has called on the students to join them at a nationwide demonstration on Saturday over working conditions and the cost of living.

rfi.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky is seeking to rally European allies at a Brussels summit on Friday after saying Kyiv would no longer abide by US President Donald Trump's demands not to strike Russian oil refineries.

rfi.description: A minibus carrying truck drivers crashed into a freight train at the loading platform of the Eurotunnel injuring 19 people, French authorities said.

rfi.title: Somalia sets date for May presidential election amid ongoing Islamist insurgency
rfi.description: Somalia's election commission has announced it will hold parliamentary and presidential polls in April and May next year, but critics say the decision will lead to more conflict in a deeply fragmented country facing a long-running Islamist insurgency.

rfi.title: War in Yemen: Houthis now ‘virtually independent’ in weapons production
rfi.description: Fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi oil and aviation targets have demonstrated the Yemeni movement’s growing military reach. Defence analyst Akram Kharief says the group has transformed its arsenal of drones and missiles since a 2022 ceasefire, building its capacity to produce weapons locally while retaining important technological links to Iran.

rfi.title: Inside Bunia’s fight to protect families from DRC’s deadliest Ebola outbreak
rfi.description: Efforts to contain Ebola are starting to pay off in Bunia, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province and epicentre of the deadliest outbreak of the disease in the country's history. More than 4,000 people have died in five months, but the response is beginning to show results, as teams work to rebuild confidence in health services, protect women and children and support survivors.

rfi.title: Infantino offers apology but 'no answers' at Fifa meeting over World Cup plan
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino gave "no satisfactory answers" when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football's global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project.

rfi.title: Challenge to HIV restrictions in French armed forces goes before top court
rfi.description: Several organisations have brought a case before France’s highest court to challenge the continued exclusion of people living with HIV from certain posts in the armed forces, gendarmerie and fire services.

rfi.title: Trial of French IS returnee highlights a growing focus on the women who came back
rfi.description: Courts are increasingly turning their attention to the women who joined the Islamic State armed group in Syria and Iraq, and then returned to France. The latest case opened Wednesday: that of Radia Tahar Aouidate, was one of 23 members of her family to travel to Syria, under the influence of her brother.

rfi.title: Belgian police raid Tshisekedi family properties in DRC mining investigation
rfi.description: Police have searched several properties in Belgium belonging to family members of Democratic Republic of Congo's President Félix Tshisekedi, as part of an investigation into suspected personal enrichment from the country’s mining sector.

rfi.title: Ukraine’s Starlink disruptions expose European reliance on US tech
rfi.description: Ukraine has reported disruptions to drones relying on Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet network, as well as the United States-operated early warning system supposed to alert it to Russian missile attacks. The problems expose Europe's dependence on US technology, with no homegrown alternatives immediately available.

rfi.title: US tech firm Nvidia buys stake in French health platform Doctolib
rfi.description: American chipmaker Nvidia has announced minority investments in four French technology companies, including the medical appointment platform Doctolib, as it expands its presence in Europe’s fast-growing artificial intelligence sector.

rfi.title: France’s emissions falling faster in 2026 but still over climate target
rfi.description: France’s greenhouse gas emissions are expected to fall by 2.8 percent in 2026, slightly more than last year – but the pace of decarbonisation remains well below what is needed to meet the country’s climate targets.

rfi.title: IMF chief says it will 'take time' to restore confidence in France's finances
rfi.description: France will need time to bring its public finances under control and fully restore investor confidence, the head of the International Monetary Fund warned on Wednesday, as rising borrowing costs put renewed pressure on the eurozone’s second-biggest economy.

rfi.title: Louvre director says major renovation plan will be ‘extremely complex’
rfi.description: Nearly a year on from a daring jewellery heist, the Louvre museum is still trying to address serious security gaps – a significant challenge for the world’s most visited museum. Its new director says a “complex” plan is under way, but the scale of the work will require further investment.

rfi.title: French National Assembly moves to overhaul response to sexual violence and abuse
rfi.description: France has taken a step towards overhauling how it tackles sexual violence after MPs passed a sweeping bill without a single vote against. It would create specialist police units and courts, abuse checks in schools and leave for victims – but protections for foreign women were dropped and the cost is still unclear.

rfi.title: French Olympic committee names flag bearers for 2026 Dakar Youth Games
rfi.description: French Olympic officials on Wednesday chose a baseball player and a rower to carry the French flag at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which begin in the Senegalese capital Dakar on 31 October.

rfi.title: Deforestation falling worldwide but Congo Basin losses grow, report finds
rfi.description: Global deforestation slowed last year, helped by gains in Latin America, but rising forest loss in Central Africa and an exceptionally strong El Nino weather pattern mean the improvement is unlikely to last, a study on Wednesday found.

euronews.title: France and Germany strike car-industry deal linking 2035 engine rules to ‘Made in Europe’ push
euronews.description: Under the agreement, carmakers would be required to cut their CO₂ emissions by 90% by 2035, without having to offset the remaining 10%, as initially proposed by the Commission.

euronews.title: Ukrainian drones force closure of all four Moscow airports overnight, cancelling dozens of flights

euronews.title: Italy: Nationwide air traffic control issues disrupt flights at Rome airport

lemonde.title: 80 ans du statut de la fonction publique : comment préserver les principes tout en faisant évoluer les pratiques
lemonde.description: Dans un contexte social et politique exigeant, la fonction publique doit se réinventer en démontrant son efficacité. Les principes d’égalité, de neutralité, mais aussi de performance, énoncés le 19 octobre 1946 dans la loi créant le premier statut républicain de ses agents, peuvent continuer de la guider.

france24fr.title: "Merci bien, Trump !" : les conservateurs du Wyoming en ordre dispersé avant les midterms
france24fr.description: Bienvenue dans le Wyoming, l’État américain le plus favorable à Donald Trump. Le républicain y a recueilli près de 70 % des suffrages lors de ses trois candidatures à la présidence. “L’État Cowboy” est le moins peuplé, le plus rural et le plus conservateur des États-Unis. À deux semaines des élections de mi-mandat, nos reporters James André et Sylvain Rousseau ont parcouru ce bastion républicain pour explorer les profondes divisions qui fracturent aujourd’hui le parti de Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : Les démocrates peuvent-ils reconquérir le vote latino ?
france24fr.description: En 2024, plus d'un électeur latino sur deux a voté pour Donald Trump. Mais depuis, ils sont de moins en moins nombreux à le soutenir, d'après les sondages. Pour comprendre ce phénomène, nous sommes allés à Phoenix, en Arizona, où les Latinos représentent plus de 40 % de la population.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ukraine en direct : "Nous sommes dépendants de Starlink", avertit Volodymyr Zelensky depuis Bruxelles
Midterms : en Arizona, les démocrates repartent à la conquête du vote latino
france24fr.description: À quelques semaines des élections de mi-mandat, les démocrates tentent de séduire l'électorat latino qui avait en partie voté pour Donald Trump en 2024. En Arizona, à Phoenix et dans sa banlieue, les difficultés économiques et la peur des expulsions pèsent sur le quotidien de cette communauté qui représente plus d'un tiers des habitants.

france24fr.title: Ukraine: Le grand lâchage ?
france24fr.description: Le conseil européen serre les rangs autour de Volodymyr Zelensky alors que Donald Trump menace d'abandonner Kiev et que Marine Le Pen: au cas où elle accéderait à l'Elysée, l'aide française à l'Ukraine prendrait fin dans les six mois suivant son élection. On va plus loin avec Niagalé Bagayoko, Anne Corpet et Caroline de Camaret à Bruxelles.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Zelensky se tourne vers l’Europe face aux incertitudes américaines
france24fr.description: Alors que les frappes russes s’intensifient et que Kiev fait face à de nombreuses coupures de courant, l’Ukraine cherche à renforcer le soutien européen. En déplacement à Bruxelles, Volodymyr Zelensky tente de consolider ses alliances, alors que le soutien américain apparaît de plus en plus incertain. À l’approche de l’hiver, les autorités ukrainiennes ont déjà annoncé des restrictions de chauffage, sur fond de nouvelles pressions sur les infrastructures énergétiques du pays. Les précisions depu

france24fr.title: Union européenne : des négociations sous tension sur le budget 2028-2034
france24fr.description: Les dirigeants européens ont entamé à Bruxelles les négociations sur le budget de l’UE pour 2028-2034, près de 2 000 milliards d’euros étant en jeu. Les discussions s’annoncent difficiles entre les pays qui réclament des coupes budgétaires et ceux qui défendent les financements agricoles et la cohésion territoriale. Autre enjeu majeur : garantir le soutien financier à l’Ukraine à partir de 2027, alors que l’appui américain devient incertain. Plusieurs États souhaitent parvenir à un accord avant

france24fr.title: Midterms : "le début de la fin du trumpisme" ?
france24fr.description: À moins de 20 jours des élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, Donald Trump multiplie les meetings pour mobiliser son électorat. Le président américain joue-t-il son avenir politique dans ce scrutin ? Le trumpisme est-il menacé ? Nous analysons également ses dernières déclarations sur l’Ukraine et sa position dans le conflit avec la Russie, avec Jim Cohen, porte-parole du Parti démocrate en France, et Randy Yaloz, avocat et porte-parole du Parti républicain en France.

france24fr.title: France : les lycéens se préparent à la mobilisation du 17 octobre, rejoints par d’autres organismes
france24fr.description: En France, les représentants des lycéens et des syndicats étudiants ont rencontré jeudi soir le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, mais jugent les échanges décevants. Depuis près d’un mois, ils se mobilisent pour réclamer davantage de moyens et de meilleures conditions d’éducation, notamment dans les lycées. Une nouvelle manifestation est prévue le 17 octobre, avec une convergence annoncée entre les mouvements lycéens, les syndicats et les Gilets jaunes.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : des perquisitions en Belgique visant l’entourage de Félix Tshisekedi
france24fr.description: Le parquet fédéral belge a mené plusieurs perquisitions à Bruxelles et dans ses environs, dans des résidences appartenant à des membres de la famille de Félix Tshisekedi, le président de la République démocratique du Congo. À l’origine de la plainte, la plateforme DESC/RDC accuse des membres du clan présidentiel de s’être illégalement approprié des mines dans la province du Katanga.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : la majorité réagit à la création du front de Joseph Kabila
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, les réactions se multiplient au sein de la majorité après la création du Front pour la refondation de la nation, dirigé par l’ancien président Joseph Kabila. Ce nouveau mouvement politico-militaire entend prendre le relais de l’AFC/M23, soutenu par le Rwanda, qui contrôle de vastes territoires dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu. Les précisions de la correspondante de France 24 à Kinshasa.

france24fr.title: Yémen : les Houthis intensifient leurs attaques contre le gouvernement
france24fr.description: Au Yémen, les rebelles houthis pro-iraniens ont frappé le palais présidentiel à Aden, faisant au moins quatre morts, dans une nouvelle escalade face au gouvernement reconnu par la communauté internationale. L’Arabie saoudite accuse l’Iran de soutenir militairement les rebelles et a riposté en frappant un site pétrolier près de Sanaa. Les combats s’intensifient également autour de plusieurs villes, dont Taëz, où les pénuries aggravent les difficultés des habitants.

france24fr.title: Georges Perec, chef d'orchestre dans Libération
france24fr.description: À la une de la presse ce vendredi 16 octobre : la préparation de la mobilisation du 17 octobre, la colère de la jeunesse ailleurs dans le monde, le climat toujours perturbé malgré la fin de l'été, et l'écrivain Georges Perec aux manettes de Libération.

france24fr.title: Argentine : la colère monte contre les coupes budgétaires dans les universités
france24fr.description: En Argentine, des manifestations contre les coupes budgétaires dans les universités publiques ont dégénéré en affrontements avec la police à Buenos Aires. Depuis son arrivée au pouvoir fin 2023, le président Javier Milei a réduit de 40 % les ressources des universités, selon une étude de l’université de Buenos Aires. Enseignants et étudiants réclament l’application d’une loi prévoyant la revalorisation des salaires et des bourses, toujours bloquée par le gouvernement au nom de l’équilibre budgét

france24fr.title: Côte d’Ivoire : un premier championnat amateur africain de MMA à Abidjan
france24fr.description: La Côte d’Ivoire accueille pour la première fois un championnat amateur africain de MMA, organisé à Abidjan par la fédération internationale Gamma. Plus de 150 athlètes venus d’une vingtaine de pays s’y affrontent pendant trois jours, avec une participation féminine en hausse. Malgré le manque de moyens et les difficultés à passer professionnel, le MMA gagne du terrain sur le continent et attire de plus en plus l’attention des fédérations internationales. Reportage de Jean Barrère.

france24fr.title: Tchad : des affrontements autour des ressources aurifères du Tibesti
france24fr.description: Depuis plusieurs jours, l’armée tchadienne affronte la principale milice présente dans la région aurifère du Tibesti. Ces combats seraient liés à un différend sur le partage des ressources minières, malgré les accords conclus par le gouvernement pour pacifier la zone. Les précisions du correspondant de France 24 Harold Girard.

france24fr.title: Maladies rénales : pourquoi l’Afrique manque de moyens pour soigner ses patients
france24fr.description: L’insuffisance rénale chronique touche des millions de personnes dans le monde, avec une prévalence particulièrement élevée en Afrique, où environ un adulte sur sept serait concerné. Faute d’accès à la dialyse et de moyens financiers, de nombreux patients meurent sans traitement ou doivent y renoncer. Le professeur Abdellatif Sidy Aly, néphrologue à Nouakchott et membre du bureau exécutif de l’Association africaine de néphrologie, revient sur ce fléau et les difficultés d’accès aux soins sur le

spiegel.title: Linke, SPD, Grüne in Berlin: Israel-Gegnerin Vanessa Emde postet ein Video - und die Ruhe ist vorbei

spiegel.description: Die Lufthansa-Tochter streicht Flüge, sagt die Weihnachtsfeier ab und prüft die Möglichkeit von Kurzarbeit im Flugbetrieb. Das wäre das erste Mal seit der Coronapandemie.

spiegel.title: Real Madrid: Super-League-Lobbyist Bernd Reichart wird Manager beim Club in Spanien
spiegel.description: Der deutsche Manager Bernd Reichart steigt in die Chefetage von Real Madrid auf. Zu den Königlichen hatte der frühere RTL-Chef schon zuvor enge Verbindungen – als Propagandist für die Super League.

spiegel.title: Kürbis: So holen Sie alles aus dem Gemüse raus – von Butternut bis Hokkaido
spiegel.description: Kürbisse sind im Herbst nicht nur dekorativ, sondern vor allem lecker. Trauen Sie sich an die Zubereitung. Selbst der Halloween-Kürbis lässt sich verwerten – zu Pumpkin Spice Latte.

spiegel.title: Ägypten: Wie Feiertage geschoben werden, um ein langes Wochenende zu gewinnen
spiegel.description: In Kairo gilt eine simple Regel: Fällt ein Feiertag ungünstig, wird er verschoben. Das klingt absurd – und folgt doch einer eigenen Alltagslogik.

spiegel.title: Lüdenscheid: 18-Jährige soll Baby aus Klinik entführt haben – Anklage erhoben
spiegel.description: Die Ermittler werfen ihr Kindesentziehung und Menschenraub vor: Eine junge Frau soll sich als Krankenhausmitarbeiterin verkleidet und einen sieben Tage alten Jungen mitgenommen haben.

spiegel.title: Zuwanderung: Arbeitsagentur warnt vor Kürzung der Migration aus dem Westbalkan
spiegel.description: Die Westbalkanregelung erleichtert seit 2016 Arbeitsuchenden den Zugang zum deutschen Arbeitsmarkt – und das erfolgreich. Trotzdem wollen Union und SPD das Kontingent kürzen. Die Wirtschaft hält das für einen Fehler.

spiegel.title: Gesundheitssystem: Alle reden von Gerechtigkeit - das größte Problem geht keiner an
spiegel.description: Fast nirgendwo geht es so ungerecht zu wie in deutschen Arztpraxen. Kassenpatienten warten ewig. Privatkunden werden bevorzugt. Das gefährdet das Grundvertrauen der Deutschen in einen fairen Staat. Die SPIEGEL-Titelstory.

spiegel.title: Elon Musk: Teslas neuer Roadster im Video – Sportwagen mit Raketenantrieb
spiegel.description: Elon Musks neuer Sportwagen beschleunigt wie eine Rakete – und fliegen kann er auch noch! Fast zehn Jahre musste die Welt auf den Tesla Roadster warten. Das Resultat im Video.

spiegel.title: Angelika Niebler: CSU-Vize legt Führungsposten im EU-Parlament nieder
spiegel.description: Angelika Niebler zählt zu den mächtigsten deutschen EU-Politikern – und geriet wegen drohender Ermittlungen unter Druck. Nun gibt sie nach SPIEGEL-Informationen ihren Führungsposten in der EVP-Fraktion ab.

spiegel.title: Japan: Behörde warnt irrtümlich vor Erdbeben der Stärke 9,9
spiegel.description: Es wäre das stärkste jemals gemessene Erdbeben gewesen: In Japan kursierte für acht Minuten eine Warnung vor extremen Erschütterungen. Tatsächlich erreichten dann Erdstöße der Stärke 1 das Land.

spiegel.description: Alle Titel der Buchreihe »Flammengeküsst« waren Bestseller, Millionen Fans weltweit warten sehnsüchtig auf die geplante Serienadaption. Nun wurden laut Medienberichten die Hauptdarsteller gecastet.

spiegel.description: Der Polizeichef wird pensioniert: Das ZDF plant einen würdigen Abschied für seinen Serienliebling Gert Achtziger, verkörpert von Alexander Duda. Der hätte bei den »Rosenheim-Cops« offenbar gern noch weitergemacht.

spiegel.title: USA: US-Senatsausschuss drängt parteiübergreifend auf Untersuchung des Starshield-Vorfalls
spiegel.description: Im US-Senat regt sich Widerstand gegen den Vorgang in der Ukraine. Auch vier Republikanerinnen und Republikaner wollen wissen, wer die Entscheidung traf, die die ukrainische Armee beeinträchtigte.

spiegel.title: Porsche: Neuer Supersportwagen »Mission S« soll 500.000 Euro kosten
spiegel.description: Elektroautos boomen, bei Porsche will man dennoch auf Verbrenner setzen. Das zeigt auch die nun vorgestellte Studie eines neuen Sportwagens: Der »Mission S« passt in mehrerlei Hinsicht zur Strategie der Stuttgarter.

observador.title: Mortes de crianças com menos de um ano aumentaram 7,7%
observador.description: Nos primeiros nove meses do ano ocorreram 195 óbitos de crianças com menos de um ano. Neste período, ocorreram 89.781 óbitos no país, menos 1.023 do que no período homólogo de 2025.

observador.description: Sindicato dos Funcionários Judiciais lembra que a carreira dos oficiais de justiça permanece sem revisão há cerca de 20 anos. A falta de profissionais é agravada pelo envelhecimento da classe.

observador.title: Tráfico humano. Empresário detido em Torre de Moncorvo

observador.title: Bragança. Detido suspeito de abuso sexual a menor

phys-org.title: Owners who spend more time close to their cats tend to have more positive moods
phys-org.description: Many owners will enthusiastically attest that their cat has improved their quality of life. Some studies support this common claim that caring for a feline friend has positive effects on human health and well-being. However, the evidence is inconsistent, and other studies have even reported possible negative effects of cat ownership.

phys-org.title: Exchange rates react immediately to the threat of tariffs
phys-org.description: Exchange rates are more than just abstract numbers. They determine the value of a Mexican peso, the cost of a German car in the U.S. and whether an Argentine farmer can repay his debts. Jantke de Boer, junior professor of international monetary macroeconomics at Ruhr University Bochum, has examined how expectations of future protectionist measures influence exchange rates.

phys-org.title: Why exposure to firearm suicide may not mean safer gun storage
phys-org.description: Knowing someone who died by firearm suicide is associated with greater recognition of suicide risk, but may not lead to safer storage practices, according to a Rutgers study published in Psychiatry Research.

phys-org.title: Solving the gallium anomaly: New calculation may explain neutrino shortfall without invoking new particles
phys-org.description: Glimpses of the "gallium anomaly" were first seen in the mid-1990s, but it was first clearly discovered and stated in 2007 by neutrino physicist Carlo Giunti of Italy. The problem is simple to state but potentially very important: about 20% fewer electron neutrinos were seen to be captured by gallium nuclei than expected.

phys-org.title: Whales take different routes but still reach dinner on time
phys-org.description: Some travelers take the scenic route. Others step on the gas and head straight for the destination. New research suggests southern right whales do much the same when crossing the Southern Ocean.

phys-org.title: Changing how you think about time could help you accomplish year-end goals: Q&A

phys-org.title: Transferable chemical prediction approach may help reduce trial and error
phys-org.description: Chemical predictions can help prevent unwanted reactions or improve the efficacy of industrial processes, among other applications, but predicting how chemicals interact can be costly and time-consuming—especially because chemicals may behave differently from one environment to another.

phys-org.title: Resistance to change has 12 different drivers, new measurement tool reveals

phys-org.title: Winter sea ice loss may be underestimated, ancient clues from a warmer Arctic suggest
phys-org.description: Future Arctic winter sea ice is likely to shrink by around 1 million square kilometers (386,000 square miles) more than previously thought, after researchers used clues from a warm period 6,000 years ago to improve the reliability of climate models.

phys-org.title: Performance under pressure: A new perspective on why we fail—or rise to the occasion
phys-org.description: The decisive penalty kick in a final, match point in tennis or the last attempt in a competition: When a lot is at stake, even a well-practiced performance can suddenly break down. Yet pressure does not necessarily impair performance. Some people perform at their best precisely in the moments that matter most. Existing accounts can only partly explain why.

phys-org.title: First in-depth map of 'forever chemicals' in the Finger Lakes created
phys-org.description: In 2023, professor Damian Helbling was getting a lot of calls and emails from local residents. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) had just announced regulations to limit per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—some of which have been linked to cancers and other negative health effects—in drinking water. Ithacans and others in the region wanted to know about levels in the ponds, lakes, streams and creeks in their proverbial backyards.

phys-org.title: Endangered species in Canada face extensive delays receiving protection
phys-org.description: For more than 20 years, Canada's Species at Risk Act (SARA) has protected wildlife that are at risk of being lost from Canadian lands and waters. Once a species is listed as extirpated, endangered or threatened under the act, it becomes illegal to kill, harm or capture it or damage its residences. Its critical habitat must also be protected, at least on federal land.

phys-org.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
phys-org.description: Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: a family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park.

phys-org.title: Can extra weight weigh on your dog's brain?
phys-org.description: Scientists have learned a lot about what happens to the human body as we age. But there's still much to learn about how other species age, including dogs. Even carrying extra weight could affect a dog's cognitive health. Alexandra Genualdi, a student at Oklahoma State University who presented her research in September at the American Physiological Society's 2026 Comparative Physiology conference in Orlando, talks about her efforts to learn more.

phys-org.title: In animated films, nonhuman characters are still overwhelmingly male
phys-org.description: Female protagonists in animated films have come a long way over the past several decades. Take the 1959 movie "Sleeping Beauty": Soft-spoken and vulnerable, Princess Aurora is cursed as an infant by the evil fairy Maleficent and ultimately saved not by her own wits, but by a prince's kiss.

phys-org.title: Newly discovered viruses reveal an evolutionary missing link
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Miami have identified a group of previously unknown viruses that bridge an evolutionary gap between viruses and cellular protein compartments, a discovery with implications for both biotechnology and scientists' understanding of the origins of life.

phys-org.title: Rigorous analysis confirms NASA's Artemis II heat shield performance
phys-org.description: NASA's Artemis II mission sent four astronauts around the moon and brought them safely back to Earth, laying a foundation for crewed flights to the moon's surface.

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm

But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

proj-syn.title: From AI Boom to Economic Bust
proj-syn.description: Contrary to tech optimists' rosy predictions, AI may prove to be a drag on growth. By concentrating wealth and economic opportunities in a few cities while destroying the low-cost jobs that have historically fueled global development, the technology could end up making much of the world poorer and more divided.

proj-syn.title: The Institutional Roots of Policy Nonsense
proj-syn.description: At a time when antimicrobial resistance threatens public health and our long-term economic well-being, tax policies favor financial engineering at the expense of developing new antibiotics. Similarly perverse incentives are at the heart of out-of-control public spending.

proj-syn.title: Is Christian Democracy Finished?
proj-syn.description: Traditionally, Christian Democrats believed that taking care of all groups in society could create a harmonious balance that would prevent instability and self-destructive infighting. But the conditions that enabled this strategy have changed, particularly in Germany, where Christian Democrats must reconnect with a different part of their history.

proj-syn.title: Independent AI Auditing Now
proj-syn.description: Recent hacking incidents confirm the need for independent scrutiny not only of what AI systems are capable of, but also of what their developers are doing to minimize harm and communicate honestly with the public. Even if AI auditing is still at an early stage, other industries have already provided a playbook.

proj-syn.title: Strict Liability for AI Executives
proj-syn.description: As an OpenAI whistleblower recently explained, AI executives have knowingly fostered a culture that “guarantees periodic failures,” the scale of which is “growing as systems get more capable.” This approach hinges on an expectation of impunity, which is why AI firms must be held legally accountable for the harm their agents cause.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Pay to Preserve Tropical Forests?
proj-syn.description: For decades, the international community has acknowledged the extraordinary value of tropical forests while failing to invest adequately in their conservation. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility, launched at last year’s United Nations Climate Change Conference, could help close this financing gap.

proj-syn.title: Why Following in Milei’s Footsteps Would Be Bad for Brazil
proj-syn.description: Far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro holds up Argentine President Javier Milei’s economic program as a model for Brazil. But Milei's economic experiment has been a failure, leaving millions of Argentinians worse off and effectively turning their heavily indebted country into a client of the United States.

proj-syn.title: How Worried Should We Be About the Global Economy?
proj-syn.description: The risks to the global economy—including high inflation, soaring public debt, market concentration, and geopolitical volatility—are well known. But it is worth underscoring just how rare and dangerous it is for all of them to be salient at the same time.

proj-syn.title: How a Pause on Frontier AI Could Work
proj-syn.description: Whether the development of frontier AI should be paused is for policymakers to decide. But they should recognize that highly concentrated hardware supply chains make a pause feasible and, if implemented properly, likely to be sustainable.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Latest Gift to Putin
proj-syn.description: Unable to win his foolish war against Iran, Donald Trump blames its consequences on Ukraine and uses the lie to justify ending sanctions against Russia, thereby extending that war as well. His diesel deal with the Kremlin is less about lowering gas prices for Americans and more about submitting to Vladimir Putin.

proj-syn.title: China’s Panda Diplomacy Is Losing Its Charm
proj-syn.description: Since giving a pair of giant pandas to the Smithsonian’s National Zoo in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s visit to Beijing, China has used panda loans as a means of projecting a harmless and friendly image globally. But it was always an act—and foreign audiences are no longer falling for it.

proj-syn.title: The Blindness of China’s All-Seeing State
proj-syn.description: China's relentless surveillance has taught people to perform obedience and loyalty, while keeping their beliefs hidden. This creates a dilemma for the ruling Communist Party: repression distorts the very information the government needs to understand society.

proj-syn.title: A Stronger Renminbi Is No Quick Fix for Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: The near-consensus among financial commentators is that China's currency is undervalued, driving global imbalances. But the renminbi's weakness reflects weak domestic demand, and pursuing currency appreciation without addressing that issue head-on would be counterproductive for everyone.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Misguided War Against Effective Altruism
proj-syn.description: The US Department of “War” has recently begun attacking effective altruism, a movement that aims to save lives, reduce suffering, and prevent future catastrophes. Why would the Trump administration, which with great fanfare created a Department of Government Efficiency, now oppose being effective?

proj-syn.title: Futureless Russia
proj-syn.description: During past periods of chaos and brutality in Russia, such as Stalin’s Great Terror, there was generally a sense that the country was headed somewhere—that the suffering served some end, however unjustifiable the means. But the repression Russians are enduring today has only one aim: to perpetuate the state that is executing it.

proj-syn.title: Public Investment Is Fiscally Responsible
proj-syn.description: Although fiscal responsibility is the right goal for any government, it cannot be properly measured through deficits and debt targets alone. Those who demand budget cuts in the face of higher debt levels overlook the importance of public spending that strengthens the economy's productive capacity over time.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of Reputation Ops
proj-syn.description: Even as most people have grown more accustomed to spotting fake news and questioning what they see online, new technologies and older tactics familiar from Cold War psyops have created a more vexing problem. Can our shared information ecosystem survive the rise of the “rep-op”?

proj-syn.title: Will the Bardella Scandal Sink Le Pen?
proj-syn.description: The scandal over antisemitic comments made by the far-right National Rally's Jordan Bardella could die down quickly, enabling Marine Le Pen to stick to her current plan: win the 2027 presidential election and name Bardella her prime minister. But there are two other possible scenarios, neither of which would be good for Bardella.
